title: Canonical liftable-point subgroup and decrease of the identity smoothness defect
statement:
All group schemes in this statement are schemes [def-pc-scheme] equipped with multiplication, identity and inverse over the indicated base, satisfying the group diagrams (the relative version of [def-sc-group-scheme]). Flatness, smoothness and local finite type have the meanings of [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A Dedekind domain is a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one. Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ for a Dedekind domain $D$, let $s$ be a closed point, and let $G$ be a flat separated $S$-group scheme locally of finite type with smooth generic fibre. Write $R=D_s$, a discrete valuation ring [lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $k=\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and choose a strict henselization $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ with residue field $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. The reduced closed subscheme (with radical defining ideals on affine charts) $F\subset G_s$ whose underlying closed subset is the closure of the images of the reductions of all $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-valued points of $G_R$ is a smooth closed $k$-subgroup scheme. For every smooth $S$-scheme $X$ and $S$-morphism $f:X\to G$, the fibre map $f_s$ factors scheme-theoretically through $F$. For the dilatation $d:G'\to G$ of $F$ at $s$ [lem-sfb-group-dilatation-universal-property], define
$$\delta_s(G)=\operatorname{length}_{R^{\mathrm{sh}}}\!\left(\operatorname{tors}_{R^{\mathrm{sh}}}\bigl(e^*\Omega^1_{G_{R^{\mathrm{sh}}}/R^{\mathrm{sh}}}\bigr)\right).$$
Here $e$ is the identity section, relative differentials and tensor pullback are [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-pc-module-pullback], $\operatorname{tors}_R(V)=\{v\in V:av=0\text{ for some }0\ne a\in R\}$, and module length is [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. This is a finite nonnegative integer, and
$$\delta_s(G')\leq\max\{0,\delta_s(G)-1\}.$$
Moreover, $\delta_s(G)=0$ if and only if $G\to S$ is smooth at the identity point $e(s)$. These conclusions require only local finite type, even if $G_s$ has infinitely many connected components; no Néron mapping property is assumed.

source.place: BLR 7.1 Lemma 4 and its proof, printed p.174, with 3.3 Lemma 1 (defect zero criterion), printed p.65; extension from finite type to locally finite type in 10.1 Proposition 4 proof, printed p.291. Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: Put $A=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and let $T\subset G_s(k^{\mathrm{sep}})$ be the reductions of $G_R(A)$. It is a subgroup, since reduction commutes with multiplication and inverse. By [lem-wf-strict-henselian-fraction-inertia], every residue automorphism lifts to an $R$-automorphism of $A$ (the displayed $\operatorname{Aut}_{R^{\mathrm h}}(A)$ isomorphism); precomposing an $A$-point with that automorphism proves that $T$ is Galois stable. Apply [lem-sfb-separable-point-closure-universal-density] to $Z=G_s$: its reduced closure $F$ is geometrically reduced, $T$ is schematically dense after extension to $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$, and $T^2$ is schematically dense in $(F_{k^{\mathrm{sep}}})^2$.

source.place: 7.1 Lemma 4 proof, opening sentence; 2.3 Proposition 11(c); 3.3 Lemma 4.

proof.text: The identity lies in $T$. On $F_{k^{\mathrm{sep}}}\times F_{k^{\mathrm{sep}}}$ every local function pulled back from the ideal of $F$ under multiplication vanishes on $T^2$, because $T$ is a subgroup; the density in step 1 makes it zero. The same argument with $T$ and inverse gives the inverse map into $F_{k^{\mathrm{sep}}}$. A $k$-linear map is zero if its scalar extension to $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ is zero (extend a nonzero vector to a basis), so the pulled-back ideal sheaves already vanish over $k$. Thus multiplication, inverse and identity factor through the closed subscheme $F$. Their group identities are inherited from $G_s$, since a closed immersion is a monomorphism. Therefore $F$ is a closed subgroup; [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth] applies to its geometric reducedness and local finite type and proves that $F/k$ is smooth.

source.place: 7.1 Lemma 4 proof: subgroup property and smoothness of the geometrically reduced group.

proof.text: Let $f:X\to G$ with $X/S$ smooth. By [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), $X_k$ and $X_{k^{\mathrm{sep}}}$ are smooth over their fields. Thus $X_k$ is geometrically reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], and [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] gives density of $X_k(k^{\mathrm{sep}})$ in $X_{k^{\mathrm{sep}}}$. Each such point lifts to $X(A)$: choose an affine open of $X_A$ containing that point; its coordinate algebra $B$ is smooth over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], and [lem-trf-henselian-smooth-algebra-lifting] applied with base and target $A$ and ideal its maximal ideal lifts $B\to k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ to $B\to A$. The image under $f$ of every lifted reduction is in $T\subset F$. A regular function on a reduced affine scheme vanishing on a dense set is zero: its nonvanishing principal open is empty, so it lies in every prime and is nilpotent, hence zero. Apply this to the pullback of the ideal of $F$ on the reduced scheme $X_{k^{\mathrm{sep}}}$, and descend its vanishing by faithful scalar extension as in step 2. This proves the scheme-theoretic factorization of $f_s$, including when $X$ is not quasi-compact.

source.place: 7.1 proof immediately before Theorem 5, printed pp.174-175; 2.3 Proposition 5 (lifting smooth points).

proof.text: Let $G_s$ be the fibre of $G_R$ over the closed point, a $k$-group scheme locally of finite type, with structure map $p_s$ and identity $e_s$. By [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change], applied to $G_R\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, the restriction $\Omega^1_{G_R/R}|_{G_s}$ (module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]) is canonically $\Omega^1_{G_s/k}$, a module of finite type. By [lem-sfb-group-scheme-differentials-from-identity], $\Omega^1_{G_s/k}\cong p_s^*e_s^*\Omega^1_{G_s/k}$; here $e_s^*\Omega^1_{G_s/k}$ is a finitely generated $k$-vector space, hence $\cong k^{r}$, and $p_s^*(k^r)=\mathcal O_{G_s}^{r}$. So $\Omega^1_{G_R/R}|_{G_s}$ is finite free, and so is its pullback to $F$ (composition of pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback]). The family $T$ is schematically dense in $F$: on an affine chart, vanishing on $T$ implies zero after scalar extension by step 1 and hence before extension. Thus $(G_R,F)$ has condition (N) of [lem-sfb-permissible-dilatation-section-estimate], with $U=F$; $F$ is smooth by step 2. All three hypotheses of the permissible-centre estimate are now established.

source.place: 7.1 Lemma 4 proof, 4.2 Proposition 2 and the two permissible-centre conditions.

proof.text: The dilatation of [lem-sfb-group-dilatation-universal-property] is flat and locally of finite type and is unchanged generically. Its identity $e'$ maps to $e$, whose closed point belongs to $T$. After localization at $s$ its chart is $B[I/\pi]$, exactly the dilatation in [lem-sfb-permissible-dilatation-section-estimate]. Hence the $A$-identity $e'$ is the unique lift of the $A$-identity $e$. Apply that estimate with $a=e$, $a'=e'$ and $U=F$ to obtain $\delta_{G_R'}(e')\leq\max\{0,\delta_{G_R}(e)-1\}$.

source.place: 7.1 Lemma 4 inequality, applying 3.3 Proposition 5 to the identity section.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change], pullback of $\Omega^1_{G_R/R}$ to $G_A$ is canonically $\Omega^1_{G_A/A}$; composition of module pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback] identifies their further pullbacks along the identity. The same applies to $G_R'$. Therefore the two lengths in step 5 are exactly $\delta_s(G)$ and $\delta_s(G')$ in the statement. Apply [lem-sfb-trait-section-differential-defect-criterion] to $X=G_R$, $a=e$: it proves that this length is a finite nonnegative integer and that it vanishes exactly when $G_R/R$ is smooth at the identity over $s$. This is equivalent to smoothness of $G/S$ at $e(s)$ by [lem-sfb-scheme-flat-smooth-point-base-change], applied to the localization $\operatorname{Spec}D_s\to\operatorname{Spec}D$; the local finite presentation hypothesis follows from [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] over the Noetherian Dedekind base. All arguments used either affine neighbourhoods of the relevant points or sheafwise vanishing. In particular none required finitely many fibre components or a Néron mapping property.

BLR is not in literature/, so each new statement was checked mathematically and on small cases. Item steps 1-6 hold. Step 1: the inertia node gives Aut_H(R^sh)=Gal, so the reduction subgroup T is Galois-stable. The two strict-henselization definitions are uniquely isomorphic. Step 2: the group law on F comes from density of T^2 and descent from k^sep to k; the geometrically-reduced lft group node then gives smoothness, and its 'every L/k' is covered. Step 3: smooth tests via base change, density of k^sep-points, the affine smooth chart and henselian lifting (0H74). The reduced-dense vanishing argument and descent are correct without quasi-compactness. Step 5: the dilatation chart B[I/pi] matches, and the identity lifts uniquely to the identity. Step 6: Omega base change plus composition of pullbacks identify the modules; the trait criterion and flat-smooth-point base change apply, with lfp from pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth. Three new nodes are true and none restates the item. The separable-point closure node: Galois-stable T is dense in Y_{k^sep}, and B into prod_T K survives tensoring with any L, which gives geometric reducedness and density of all products; T empty is allowed. The defect criterion is BLR 3.3/1; I proved both directions using equidimensionality of the flat integral component. The permissible estimate is general BLR 3.3/5; tested on xy=pi^2 at (pi,pi), where the defect goes from 1 to 0, and on smooth X. FIX (C5 duplicate): the new node lem-sfb-group-invariant-cotangent-trivialization restates Stacks 047I, which the existing same-unit node lem-sfb-group-scheme-differentials-from-identity states over a field. The item only needs Omega restricted to G_s to be finite free. I dropped the node and step 4 now cites lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change, def-pc-module-pullback and the field node, with the finite-free argument written out; proof_deps is recomputed and there is no cycle.
